title: Tech Note: Power your ORDA queries with query options
author: Xiang Liu, Technical Services Team Member, 4D Inc.

historical_commentary.text: dataClass.query() and its query-string syntax (attributePath/comparator/value/logicalOperator, IN, NOT, dot-notation relations) remain the core, still-current way to query ORDA data classes in 4D today; this note's best practices around NOT, EXCEPT, and null-handling are still accurate and useful, though some 'undocumented' options mentioned may since have been formally documented as ORDA matured.
related_updates: ORDA's query() syntax has remained stable and is 4D's standard modern query API, now fully documented including options this note called undocumented at the time
classic QUERY/QUERY BY ATTRIBUTE commands still exist for non-ORDA/array-based code but ORDA query() is the recommended approach for entity-based data access
